text.p: New York-based bank holding firm Chase Manhattan Corp on Tuesday opened its first branch office in China's booming city of Shanghai and officials said the next step would be to seek a licence for local currency business.

The branch would expand on business done by Chase's Shanghai representative office, which had engaged in securities and debt underwriting, loan syndications and risk management, said Peter Shay, general manager of the new branch.

Chase would soon move the office to Shanghai's Pudong New Area as the first step in securing Beijing's blessing to conduct local renminbi currency business, and as part of the bank's drive to become a major player in China's financial markets, Murck said.

The bank was also seeking a local currency licence for its branch in Tianjin and hoped to win a branch licence for Beijing, a process that would take at least a year from the opening of the Shanghai branch because of Chinese rules, he said.

Currently only nine foreign banks are allowed to do renminbi business in China, which has limited the banks' business scope and requires them to set up their main branch offices in Pudong, across the Huangpu River from central Shanghai.
